title: Classifying Living Things
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Classifying Living Things Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe biodiversity as the variety of life; classify organisms into groups (kingdoms, vertebrates and invertebrates) using their characteristics; use and make dichotomous keys. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Biodiversity)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 science worksheets on biodiversity, kingdoms, vertebrates, invertebrates and dichotomous keys, with Ontario plants and animals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Scientists group living things by features.
key_sub: Vertebrates have a backbone; keys split groups in two at each step.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biodiversity is the variety of living things. Classification sorts them into groups by shared features.

  • Kingdoms include animals, plants and fungi (and tiny living things like bacteria).
  • Vertebrates have a backbone: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
  • Invertebrates have no backbone: insects, spiders, worms, snails.
  • A dichotomous key asks yes-or-no questions to name a living thing.
Example

A frog has moist skin and starts life as a tadpole. Which group is it in?

moist skin

water then land

Answer: amphibians

Example

Is a spider an insect?

count the legs: 8

Answer: no, it is an arachnid

Common mistakes

  • Thinking spiders are insects.
  • Thinking whales are fish (they are mammals).
  • Thinking fungi are plants.

faq.a: The variety of living things in an area, from tiny insects to large trees and animals.

faq.q: What is the difference between vertebrates and invertebrates?
faq.a: Vertebrates have a backbone. Invertebrates do not.

faq.q: How does a dichotomous key work?
faq.a: It gives two choices at each step. You choose the one that fits until you reach the name.

items.q: Which group of living things does the bacteria that cause food poisoning belong to?
items.e: Bacteria are living things too small to be seen without a microscope.

items.q: Which group has a backbone?
items.e: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals have backbones.

items.q: Which group of living things does a hibiscus plant belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which group does a squid belong to?
items.e: A squid has a soft body: a mollusc.

items.q: Which tree is a conifer?
items.e: Conifers have cones and needles.

items.q: Which group of living things does a bracket fungus belong to?
items.e: Fungi cannot make their own food. They feed on dead or decaying matter and reproduce by spores.

items.q: An animal has a hard outer shell and many jointed legs, and most live in water. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of crustaceans.

items.q: Which group does a goldfish belong to?
items.e: A goldfish is a fish.

items.q: A dichotomous key gives two choices at each step. What do you do?
c: pick the choice that matches the living thing and follow it
items.e: Each step splits the group in two.

items.q: What is a species?
c: a group of living things that can breed and have young that can also breed
items.e: Moose are one species.

items.q: Which group does a crab belong to?
items.e: A crab is a crustacean.

items.q: Which group does a grasshopper belong to?
items.e: A grasshopper is an insect.

items.q: Which group does a swan belong to?
items.e: A swan is a bird.

items.q: Which animal is an invertebrate?
items.e: Invertebrates have no backbone.

items.q: Which group does a spider belong to?
items.e: Spiders have 8 legs and 2 body parts: arachnids, not insects.

items.q: Which is a vertebrate that lives in Ontario lakes?
items.e: Fish have backbones.

items.q: Which group does a crocodile belong to?
items.e: A crocodile is a reptile.

items.q: An animal has eight jointed legs and no antennae. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of arachnids.

items.q: An animal has a hard outer skeleton, two pairs of antennae and lots of legs. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of crustaceans.

items.q: Which group of living things does the bacteria that cause tooth decay belong to?
items.e: Bacteria are living things too small to be seen without a microscope.

items.q: Which of these animals is a fish?
items.e: A trout is a fish.

items.q: Which group are spiders in?
items.e: Spiders have two body parts and eight legs.

items.q: A painted turtle has dry scaly skin and lays eggs on land. Which vertebrate group is it in?
items.e: Reptiles have dry scales.

items.q: Which of these animals is a crustacean?
items.e: A shrimp is a crustacean.

items.q: Is an owl a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. An owl is a bird.

items.q: Which of these animals is a crustacean?
items.e: Barnacles are crustaceans that stick to rocks.

items.q: Which of these animals is a fish?
items.e: A salmon is a fish.

items.q: Which kingdom makes its own food using sunlight?
items.e: Plants are producers.

items.q: Which feature do all mammals share?
c: They have hair or fur and feed their young milk.
items.e: Beavers and bats are mammals.

items.q: Is a barnacle a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. Barnacles are crustaceans that stick to rocks.

items.q: Is an axolotl a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. Axolotls are amphibians that keep their gills.

items.q: Which of these animals is an insect?
items.e: A grasshopper is an insect.

items.q: Is an ostrich a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. Ostriches cannot fly, but they have feathers: birds.

items.q: Is a bat a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. Bats have fur and feed their young on milk: mammals, not birds.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the flying fox belong to?
items.e: A placental mammal is a mammal whose young grow inside the mother, fed by a placenta.

items.q: Mushrooms do not make their own food and grow from spores. Which kingdom are they in?
items.e: Fungi absorb food from what they grow on.

items.q: Is a seal a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. Seals have fur, breathe air and feed their young on milk.

items.q: Which feature do all insects share?
c: six legs and three body parts
items.e: Spiders have eight legs, so they are not insects.

items.q: Is a squid a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A squid has a soft body: a mollusc.

items.q: Which of these animals is an arachnid?
items.e: Harvestmen have 8 legs: arachnids.

items.q: An animal has feathers. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has feathers belongs to the birds.

items.q: An animal breathes through lungs and lays eggs with leathery shells on land. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that breathes through lungs and lays eggs with leathery shells on land belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: How many legs does a crab have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group small creatures: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: How many legs does a harvestman have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group small creatures: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: How many legs does a beetle have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group small creatures: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: How many legs does a slug have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group small creatures: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: Which group of animals does a stingray belong to?
items.e: A stingray has scales and fins, so it belongs to the fish.

items.q: Which group of animals does a cobra belong to?
items.e: A cobra has dry, scaly skin, so it belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: Which group of animals does a sparrow belong to?
items.e: A sparrow has feathers, so it belongs to the birds.

items.q: Which group of animals does a tilapia belong to?
items.e: A tilapia has scales and fins, so it belongs to the fish.

items.q: Is a rose a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A rose makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: An animal has moist skin without scales. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has moist skin without scales belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: Is a moss a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A moss does not make flowers. It reproduces with spores.

items.q: Is a liverwort a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A liverwort does not make flowers. It reproduces with spores.

items.q: Which group of animals does a salamander belong to?
items.e: A salamander has moist skin without scales, so it belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: Is a dandelion a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A dandelion makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: Which group of animals does a frog belong to?
items.e: A frog has moist skin without scales, so it belongs to the amphibians.

items.q: An animal lays eggs with hard shells. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that lays eggs with hard shells belongs to the birds.

items.q: An animal has three body parts and six legs. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has three body parts and six legs belongs to the insects.

items.q: Is a fir tree a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A fir tree does not make flowers. It reproduces with seeds in cones.

items.q: Maya's key asks 'Is it big?' Why is this a poor question?
c: Big is not exact, so different people may answer differently.
items.e: Use measurable features.

items.q: Why do scientists use characteristics rather than habitat to classify animals?
c: Animals in the same habitat can be very different, such as a shark and a whale.
items.e: Shared features show relationships.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: axolotl, newt, salamander, wasp?
items.e: The other three are amphibians; a wasp is one of the insects.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: turtle, duck, tortoise, cobra?
items.e: The others are reptiles. A duck belongs to the birds.

items.q: A newly found animal has fur, breathes air and feeds its young milk, but lives in the sea. How should it be classified?
items.e: Classify by characteristics, not by where it lives.

items.q: How could you improve the question 'Does it have lots of legs?'
c: Ask 'Does it have legs or not legs?'
Change it to 'Does it have more than six legs?'
items.e: Make it precise.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: shark, stingray, goldfish, owl?
items.e: The others are fish. An owl belongs to the birds.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: frog, salamander, toad, cat?
items.e: The others are amphibians. A cat belongs to the mammals.

items.q: A key for trees uses leaf shape. Why is this useful in winter for evergreen trees but not oak trees?
c: Oak trees lose their leaves in fall.
Oak trees have no leaves ever.
items.e: Choose features you can see.

items.q: Which question would sort a bee from a spider?
items.e: Choose a feature that only one has.

items.q: Why might two scientists classify the same plant differently at first?
c: They might choose different characteristics to group by.
items.e: Classification is based on chosen features.

items.q: Two animals reach the same end of a key. What does this show?
c: The key needs another question to separate them.
items.e: Improve the key.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: bee, grasshopper, ladybug, tortoise?
items.e: The other three are insects; a tortoise is one of the reptiles.
